title: Turn each key/value pair into a JSON property.
hint: Record I", then f= and s": ", then A",. Finish with j0 and replay twice.
why: A delimiter motion finds each key boundary; line-end insertion handles values of different lengths.

title: Change each Markdown heading into a bullet.
hint: Record ct followed by Space, type -, then Escape and j0.
why: Changing up to the first space handles a varying number of heading markers without counting them.

title: Keep only the middle field of each CSV record.
hint: Record df, to remove the first field; f,D removes the remaining comma and tail. End with j0.
why: Separate delimiter-based operations extract a field without depending on its width.

title: Move each trailing comma to the beginning of its row.
hint: Record $x to cut the comma, 0P to put it before the row, then j0.
why: A one-character delete and put can move punctuation without entering Insert mode.

title: Convert each assignment into a function call.
hint: Record f=r(, then A); and Escape. Finish with j0.
why: Character replacement preserves the value, while a separate suffix insertion closes the new syntax.

title: Remove the enclosing quotes from each line.
hint: Record 0x$xj0, then replay twice.
why: When the exact enclosing structure is guaranteed, boundary operations avoid touching spaces inside the value.

title: Swap the first two words on every line.
before:
red apple ripe
green pear crisp
yellow lemon tart
after:
apple red ripe
pear green crisp
lemon yellow tart
hint: Record daw to cut the first word, wP to place it before the third, then j0.
why: Around-word deletion carries its separator, allowing the moved word to fit between existing words.

title: Duplicate each configuration row directly below itself.
after:
host=local
host=local
port=8080
port=8080
mode=dev
mode=dev
hint: Record yypj0: copy, put below, then move past the copy to the next original row.
why: A macro that grows the buffer must advance relative to the inserted text so it does not keep duplicating the same row.

title: Turn each two-line name/email record into one CSV row.
before:
Ada
ada@example.com
Lin
lin@example.com
Lee
lee@example.com
hint: Record A,, Escape, gJ, j0; replay twice.
why: Joining without added whitespace converts paired lines into a delimited record.

title: Copy each setting name into its own quoted value.
hint: Record yiw, f", p, then j0.
why: Yanking inside the macro refreshes the register on every replay, so each row supplies its own value.

title: Collapse repeated spaces between these words to one.
hint: Use :%s/  */ /g: a space followed by space-star, replaced by one space.
why: A repeated-space pattern consumes a run in one match instead of removing individual spaces unpredictably.

title: Wrap each ERROR label in square brackets.
before:
ERROR disk
WARN cache
ERROR network
hint: Use :%s/^ERROR/[&]/.
why: & inserts the entire matched text into the replacement; the anchor limits wrapping to a leading label.

title: Replace each literal dollar sign with “USD ”.
hint: Use :%s/\$/USD /g.
why: Escaping $ matches the currency character rather than the end-of-line anchor.

title: Remove the leading indentation from the pasted snippet.
why: A start anchor restricts the whitespace match to indentation; spaces within content would remain intact.

title: Replace each pipe separator with a comma, leaving spaces intact.
why: A character class matches the literal pipe consistently, avoiding its alternation meaning in some regex modes.

title: Remove a single optional “# ” prefix on these lines.
why: Lines without a match remain unchanged; substitution can clean a mixed commented/uncommented block.

title: Replace only two-digit revision codes with “XX”.
why: The equals sign and end anchor constrain the entire numeric field to exactly two digits.

title: Remove empty parentheses at the ends of these names.
hint: Use :%s/[(][)]$//. Character classes match the literal parentheses.
why: Literal delimiter classes and the end anchor remove only empty call suffixes, preserving calls with arguments.

title: Remove records whose status field is exactly “SKIP”.
before:
KEEP build
SKIP docs
SKIPPING label
SKIP lint
KEEP test
after:
KEEP build
SKIPPING label
KEEP test
hint: Use :g/^SKIP /d, including the space after SKIP.
why: The field separator prevents the pattern from also matching SKIPPING.

title: Remove whitespace-only separator lines.
hint: Use :g/^ *$/d.
why: The star allows zero or more spaces, so both empty and space-only lines match.

title: Change the retry value on the line ending in “# production” to 5.
before:
retries=2 # development
retries=3 # production
retries=1 # test
after:
retries=2 # development
retries=5 # production
retries=1 # test
hint: Find production$, then 0f=l reaches the numeric value.
why: A distinctive trailing annotation can locate a record even when its key is repeated.

title: Delete the line immediately above the END marker.
before:
keep
remove this note
END
footer
hint: Search for the exact marker, move up, and delete that line.
why: A nearby stable marker can identify the edit location when the text to remove has no useful pattern.

title: Insert “verify();” directly before “deploy();”.
hint: Search for ^deploy, then O opens a line above.
why: Search plus O inserts relative to a semantic landmark without knowing its line number.

title: Delete the final standalone “temp”, leaving “template”.
hint: With the cursor on the first temp, * finds the next whole-word match; dd removes its line.
why: Whole-word search excludes template before a linewise edit.

title: Uppercase the earlier “warn” label, leaving the current one alone.
before:
warn early
info middle
warn late
after:
WARN early
info middle
warn late
hint: Use # to find the preceding whole-word match, then gUiw.
why: Search direction controls which occurrence receives the operator.

title: Clear the arguments of the first call after the setup section.
hint: Find run, move to its parenthesis, then di(.
why: Searching for the function name and editing its argument object preserves other calls.

title: Change the previous chapter heading to uppercase.
before:
chapter one
body
chapter two
body
after:
chapter one
body
CHAPTER TWO
body
hint: Search backward for ^chapter, then gUU uppercases its line.
why: An anchored backward search is useful when editing a section from somewhere inside it.

title: Replace the last matching status with “done”.
before:
status: queued
status: running
status: waiting
after:
status: queued
status: running
status: done
hint: From the first line, the search finds the second; n reaches the third. Find its colon and change the tail.
why: Repeated search and a local delimiter motion isolate the last field without modifying the earlier records.

title: Remove the bracketed tag from the urgent message.
hint: Find urgent, delete around its brackets, then x removes the leftover space.
why: A search result can position an enclosing text-object edit, including its delimiters.

title: Change the number after “limit” to 20, preserving the earlier version.
hint: Search for limit, then move after its equals sign and replace the number.
why: Searching for the key avoids accidentally editing the first number on the same line.

title: Replace only the inner list with “ready”.
hint: Use ci[ while inside the list.
why: The nearest bracket object is independent of the surrounding function arguments.

title: Clear the inner object without changing the outer one.
hint: Use di{ inside the nested object.
why: Cursor placement chooses the nearest enclosing brace pair.

title: Replace the bold text inside the paragraph.
hint: Use cit with the cursor in world.
why: The nearest tag pair is strong, so the surrounding paragraph stays intact.

title: Remove the nested emphasis but keep the surrounding link.
hint: Use dat from inside this.
why: Around-tag deletion removes the whole em element. The leading space inside the element is removed along with the emphasized text.

title: Replace the entire URL with “/health”.
hint: Use ciW inside the URL.
why: A WORD object treats punctuation as part of the whitespace-delimited URL.

title: Delete the quoted argument and its following comma-space.
hint: Use da" inside the quoted argument, then xx removes the comma and space.
why: Around-quotes includes the string delimiters but not its argument separator.

title: Lowercase only the identifier inside parentheses.
hint: Use gui( inside the parentheses.
why: Case operators accept text objects, preserving the call and its delimiters.

title: Replace the backtick command while preserving the surrounding text.
hint: Use ci` inside the code span.
why: A delimiter object handles spaces within the inline command.

title: Delete the first paragraph but keep the heading above it.
before:
# Notes

Obsolete explanation.
More obsolete details.

Current explanation.
hint: Use dap from inside the obsolete paragraph.
why: The paragraph object keeps the separate heading and removes the following separator with the obsolete text.

title: Replace only the final component of “user.name”.
hint: Use ciw with the cursor in name.
why: A small-word object stops at punctuation, unlike a WORD object that would include user.name.

title: Replace the three aligned dashes with colons.
before:
key - value
foo - bar
zip - zap
after:
key : value
foo : bar
zip : zap
hint: Select the column with Ctrl+v and 2j, then r:.
why: A rectangular replacement changes the separator column without touching either field.

title: Remove the “// ” prefixes from the three indented calls.
hint: Select three columns across three lines, then d.
why: Starting the rectangle after indentation preserves the alignment of the uncommented code.

title: Lowercase only the four-letter status column.
before:
PASS alpha
FAIL beta
PASS gamma
after:
pass alpha
fail beta
pass gamma
hint: Select four columns across three rows, then u.
why: Visual-block case conversion can normalize a fixed-width field independently of its neighbors.

title: Replace the second list with a copy of the first list’s contents.
hint: Yank inside the first brackets into a, select inside the second, and put a.
why: An explicit register separates the text you want to reuse from the text replaced by a visual put.

title: Swap “alpha” and “beta” while keeping the equals signs.
hint: Save alpha in a and beta in b, then replace each word using the opposite register.
why: Two named registers let you exchange values without losing either one.

title: Copy the first two words to the end of the line.
hint: Yank two words, append a space, then put and remove the trailing separator.
why: Wordwise yanks can include a trailing space; a precise target may require cleaning that separator.

title: Bring the two-line note under the heading.
before:
Notes
body
separator
line one
line two
END
after:
Notes
line one
line two
body
separator
END
hint: Mark the heading, cut two lines above END, return with 'a, and put.
why: A named destination survives the line-number changes caused by cutting a block.

title: Convert the array brackets to parentheses without changing the contents.
hint: Jump to the matching bracket with %, replace it, then replace the opening bracket.
why: Matching-pair motion is safer than counting characters to reach the closing delimiter.

title: Replace both quoted arguments with empty strings.
hint: Delete inside the first quotes, find the comma and next opening quote, then delete inside the second.
why: After shrinking the first value, use delimiters to find the second instead of its old column.

title: Indent the inner two statements and add semicolons.
hint: Select the two lines and shift right; append a semicolon and repeat on the other line.
why: A block operation and dot repeat can handle independent formatting changes without retyping the statements.
